memory:
I've been taking medication for diabetes, hypertension, osteoarthritis, and hypothyroidism. I've had to adjust my medication regimen several times to find what works best for me. It's crucial to keep track of all my medications and their dosages to avoid any mistakes or missed doses. Regular reviews with my doctor help us identify any necessary adjustments to my medication plan.

For my hypertension, I've been taking lisinopril 10 mg daily for years. It helps keep my blood pressure under control, and my doctor is happy with my current readings. I also make sure to monitor my blood pressure at home regularly to ensure it stays within a healthy range.

For my osteoarthritis, I've been taking celecoxib(Celebrex) 200 mg twice daily for several years. It helps reduce pain and inflammation in my joints, allowing me to stay active and mobile. I also use a heating pad or take a warm bath with Epsom salts to relieve stiffness and discomfort. My doctor recommended trying tai chi or gentle stretching exercises to further improve joint health.

For my hypothyroidism, I've been taking levothyroxine(Synthroid) 100 mcg daily for years. It helps regulate my thyroid function and keeps my TSH levels in the normal range. I make sure to get regular check-ups with my doctor to monitor my thyroid function and adjust my medication as needed.

I've been taking losartan 50 mg once daily for my high blood pressure. It's been keeping my readings mostly in the 135-140/80-90 mmHg range, which is a bit higher than ideal. My doctor suggests that stress management and reducing sodium intake can help instead of increasing the dosage. I also take a daily magnesium supplement, which I've heard can help with blood pressure regulation.

I've been taking levothyroxine 75 mcg every morning for my hypothyroidism. It's been stable for years, and my last TSH test came back at 2.1 mIU/L, which is within the normal range. I make sure to take it on an empty stomach and wait at least 30 minutes before eating. If I miss a dose, I feel sluggish the next day, so I keep a pill organizer to stay on track.

I've been taking acetaminophen as needed for mild pain from osteoarthritis. When my joints are really acting up, my doctor prescribed meloxicam 7.5 mg, an anti-inflammatory. I don't take it every day because I don't want to overdo it on NSAIDs, but it definitely helps when my knees and hands are particularly stiff. My doctor also suggested trying glucosamine supplements, but I can't say for sure if they've made a difference.

I've been taking vitamin D3 2,000 IU daily to boost my vitamin D levels, which were found to be low at 22 ng/mL. I also take calcium supplements since my last bone density scan showed early signs of osteopenia. My doctor recommended combining it with vitamin K2 to help with absorption.

I've been taking atorvastatin 10 mg daily as a statin to help with my cholesterol. My LDL was a bit high at 130 mg/dL, and my triglycerides were at 140 mg/dL, so my doctor thought a low-dose statin would be beneficial. So far, my cholesterol numbers have been improving, and I haven't experienced any side effects, which is a relief since some people report muscle aches with statins.

I've been taking a daily multivitamin to ensure I'm getting all the necessary nutrients. I also take omega-3 supplements to support heart health and probiotics to help with digestion. Since my gallbladder was removed a few years ago, I sometimes take digestive enzymes if I eat something heavier. Losing my gallbladder changed the way I digest fatty foods, so I have to be mindful of that.

One thing I keep an eye on is potential medication interactions. Since I take both losartan and meloxicam occasionally, my doctor warned me that NSAIDs can sometimes affect kidney function, so I try not to take meloxicam too often. I also make sure to take my thyroid medication separately from my calcium and iron supplements, since they can interfere with absorption.

Overall, I think my medication routine is working well for me. It's a lot to keep track of, but I make sure to stay organized with a pill planner and use reminders on my phone. I also try to focus on lifestyle changes, so I don't have to rely on medications alone. My goal is to stay as healthy as possible and avoid unnecessary prescriptions by managing things naturally when I can!
